content.title: Terms of Usage
content.meta: Operator: Adwiti Technocrats Pvt. Ltd · Effective Date: 15-September-2026 · Contact: Contact Us

sections.title: 1. Definitions
sections.body:
• Custodian: The sovereign administrator of the Platform, who does not participate as a Trader, Market Maker, or TSX Master in any transaction.
  • TradeSphereX / TSX: A whitelisted storefront on the Platform under its own branding, administered by a TSX Master.
  • TSX Master: A person authorised by a TSX's company, under formal agreement with ADWITIX, to administer that TSX's storefront.
  • Trader: A registered user who bids on, offers for, or purchases a Lot.
  • Market Maker: A registered user approved by a specific TSX to list items for sale on that TSX's storefront.
  • Lot: A cataloged item and its associated description, media, and condition information.
  • Sale System: The transactional format under which a Lot is offered — Buy-Now, Express Auction, Easy Auction, or Tender Auction.
  • EMD: A refundable security deposit pledged by a Trader to participate in a bid or offer, calculated as 10% of the applicable value.
  • PC / Money Points: The Platform's internal representation of a Trader's deposited funds, held at 1:1 parity, maintained as segregated per-pledge escrow holdings rather than a pooled or freely spendable balance. PC is never used to pay for goods directly.
  • RV / EV: Reserve Value and Expected Value — the floor and target prices set by a Market Maker for a Lot.
  • NOC: A digital No Objection Certificate confirming, respectively, receipt of funds (Market Maker) or receipt of goods (Trader).
  • Star Rating: The Platform's dual, independent reputation scores — Trader★ and Market Maker★ — reflecting a user's transaction history.

sections.title: 2. Eligibility & Registration
sections.body:
2.1. You must be at least 18 years of age and capable of entering into a legally binding contract under Indian law to register for or use the Platform.

2.2. Registration requires a valid 10-digit Indian mobile number, verified by OTP. You are responsible for the confidentiality of your account credentials, including your 4-digit mPIN.

2.3. Each user may hold only one account, uniquely tied to their verified mobile number. Creating multiple accounts, or registering on behalf of another person without authorisation, is prohibited.

2.4. You agree to provide accurate, current, and complete information during registration and KYC verification, and to promptly update it if it changes.

2.5. Business/organisational users must additionally provide corporate verification details (CIN, GSTIN, company PAN) as prescribed by KYC requirements.

sections.title: 3. Account Security
sections.body:
3.1. You are solely responsible for all activity under your account, whether or not authorised by you, except where it results from the Platform's own security failure.

3.2. You must notify the Platform immediately if you suspect unauthorised access to your account.

3.3. Three consecutive failed mPIN attempts trigger a mandatory OTP verification step before further access is permitted.

sections.title: 4. Nature of the Platform
sections.body:
4.1. ADWITIX is a marketplace facilitator only. We are not a party to, and assume no responsibility for, the underlying sale contract between a Trader and a Market Maker. Title to any item transfers directly between them, not through the Platform.

4.2. The Platform does not take custody of, inspect, or guarantee the condition, legality, or authenticity of any Lot, except as expressly stated in these Terms (e.g., mandatory listing media requirements).

4.3. 100% of the sale value for any completed transaction is settled directly and offline between Trader and Market Maker. The Platform never holds, transmits, or has custody of the full sale value — only the EMD (where applicable) is held via the Platform's payment mechanisms.

4.4. The Custodian does not participate as a Trader, Market Maker, or TSX Master in any transaction, and has no visibility into live bidding activity while it is in progress.

sections.title: 5. Bidding, EMD & Settlement
sections.body:
5.1. A Trader must pledge an EMD of 10% of the applicable value before placing a bid or offer. The EMD is refunded automatically once no longer required (outbid, not selected, or deal closed with balance remaining).

5.2. A winning Trader who fails to complete payment within the applicable window forfeits their EMD. The win passes to the next-highest bidder (Baton-Pass), up to three times, before the Trading Session is cancelled.

5.3. Both parties must file an NOC before a deal is considered closed — the Market Maker confirming receipt of funds, the Trader confirming receipt of goods.

sections.title: 6. Star Ratings, Crawl-Back & Shadow Banning
sections.body:
6.1. Every user holds two independent Star Ratings — Trader★ and Market Maker★ — starting at 3.0 of 5.0, rising with clean conduct and falling with defaults or disputes.

6.2. A rating below 2★ enters Crawl-Back (restricted to smaller-value transactions); a persistently low rating may result in Shadow Banning (reduced visibility, not a block).

sections.title: 7. Disputes & Termination
sections.body:
7.1. Disputes are handled under our separate Dispute Resolution Process. A TSX Master ruling may be appealed once, to the Custodian, whose decision is final.

7.2. We may suspend or terminate your account for breach of these Terms, fraud, repeated non-payment, or as required by law, with a stated reason.

sections.title: 8. Governing Law
sections.body: 8.1. These Terms are governed by the laws of India. Disputes not resolved through our internal process are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts at [city — TODO].

sections.title: 9. Changes to These Terms
sections.body: 9.1. We may update these Terms from time to time. Material changes will be reflected in the "Effective Date" above and, where required, notified to you directly.

content.footer: See also our Privacy Policy and Trust & Support.

content.title: Privacy Policy
content.meta: Data Fiduciary: Adwiti Technocrats Pvt. Ltd · Effective Date: 15-September-2026 · Contact (Grievance/Data Protection): Contact Us

sections.title: 1. Introduction & Scope
sections.body:
1.1. This Privacy Policy describes how ADWITIX ("the Platform", "we", "us") collects, uses, discloses, and protects the personal data of registered Traders, Market Makers, and TSX Masters ("you") in connection with your use of the Platform.

1.2. This Policy applies across all TradeSphereX storefronts operating on the Platform. Individual TSXs may not collect or process your personal data outside the mechanisms described here without your separate consent.

1.3. By registering for or using the Platform, you consent to the collection and processing of your personal data as described in this Policy.

sections.title: 2. Data We Collect
sections.body:
2.1 Identity & Contact: Mobile number (verified via OTP, your unique identifier), full name, salutation, date of birth, email address (where provided).

2.2 KYC & Verification: Individuals — PAN, Aadhaar (masked/tokenised), occupation. Businesses — CIN, GSTIN, company PAN, MSME/UDYAM registration, company type, industry, and optionally turnover/employee count. Supporting documents as applicable to your account type.

2.3 Address & Banking: Up to four address records (Registered, Billing, Correspondence, Site/Yard) with optional GPS. Encrypted banking details for refunds and settlements.

2.4 Transactional: Lots, bids, offers, EMD pledges/refunds, settlement records, NOC confirmations, Star Rating history, and disclosed reasons for withdrawals, rejections, disputes, or rating downgrades.

2.5 Listing Media & Location: Photographs, videos, and documents uploaded for a Lot, including GPS/timestamp data captured at the moment of upload for authenticity verification.

2.6 Device & Usage: IP address, browser/device type, session activity, and login timestamps, collected automatically for security and audit purposes.

sections.title: 3. How We Use Your Data
sections.body:
• To create and authenticate your account, and verify your identity (KYC).
  • To operate the Platform's core functions: Lots, bidding, EMD management, settlement, and Star Ratings.
  • To detect and prevent fraud, including phishing/circumvention monitoring, duplicate accounts, and bid manipulation.
  • To personalise your experience, including CAT-LOC-VAL matching and notification delivery.
  • To communicate with you regarding transactions, disputes, and account status.
  • To comply with applicable legal, tax, and regulatory obligations, including audit and retention requirements.
  • To generate aggregated, de-identified analytics that do not identify any individual user.

sections.title: 4. Data Sharing & Disclosure
sections.body:
4.1 Within the Platform

RecipientWhat They See
TSX MasterListings, bid/offer history, and identity details of users transacting on their own storefront, strictly as needed for approval, dispute, and compliance functions — bidder identity stays masked during live bidding.
Market Maker (completed transaction)The winning Trader's identity and contact details, revealed only upon acceptance of an offer or close of a Trading Session.
Trader (completed transaction)The Market Maker's identity, location, and inspection contact details, revealed upon EMD pledge or offer acceptance.
CustodianFull transaction records for audit purposes, accessible only after a Trading Session concludes — no visibility into live bidding.

4.2 Third-Party Service Providers: identity/authentication providers (Custodian multi-factor authentication), SMS/communication providers (OTP and alerts), payment gateway and bank verification providers (EMD processing), cloud infrastructure providers (hosting, media, backup), AI service providers (advisory listing-quality pre-checks, limited to listing content, excluding KYC data). These providers are contractually bound to process your data only for the purposes we specify.

4.3 Legal & Regulatory: We may disclose your data where required by law, regulation, court order, or governmental authority, including tax, anti-money-laundering, or audit obligations.

4.4 What We Do Not Do: We do not sell your personal data to any third party. We do not share your KYC documents with any TSX or other user — TSX Masters see only your verification status, never the underlying documents.

sections.title: 5. Data Security & Retention
sections.body:
5.1. Sensitive identity data is encrypted and tokenised at rest. Banking details are encrypted and used solely for refunds and settlements.

5.2. We retain your data for as long as your account is active, and thereafter for the period required by applicable tax, audit, and regulatory obligations.

sections.title: 6. Your Rights
sections.body: 6.1. Subject to applicable law, you may request access to, correction of, or erasure of your personal data, by contacting the Data Protection contact above. Some data (e.g., transaction and audit records) may be retained despite an erasure request where required by law.

sections.title: 7. Changes to This Policy
sections.body: 7.1. We may update this Policy as our data practices change. Material changes will be reflected in the "Effective Date" above.

content.footer: See also our Cookie Policy and Terms of Usage.

content.title: Refund & Cancellation Policy
content.meta: Adwiti Technocrats Pvt. Ltd · Effective Date: 15-September-2026 · Contact: Contact Us

sections.title: 1. Scope
sections.body: 1.1. This Policy explains when an EMD is refunded, when it is forfeited, and how Lot or Trading Session cancellations are handled on ADWITIX. It should be read together with our Fee & Charges Schedule and Terms of Usage.

sections.title: 2. EMD Refunds
sections.body:
2.1. An EMD pledged on a bid or offer is refunded in full, automatically, the moment it is no longer required — for example, when a Trader is outbid, not selected, or a transaction formally closes with a balance remaining.

2.2. Refunds are processed as soon as operationally possible. No fixed turnaround time is guaranteed, though refunds are not intentionally delayed.

2.3. Any Payment Gateway collection charge added at the time of deposit is not itself refunded, as it is a pass-through charge for processing the original transaction, not a platform fee.

sections.title: 3. Forfeiture (When a Deposit Is Not Refunded)
sections.body:
3.1. If a winning Trader fails to complete payment within the applicable window, their EMD is forfeited in full — this is not a refundable event.

3.2. In a standard default, the forfeited amount is applied first to platform/TSX commission, with the remainder passed to the Market Maker as compensation.

3.3. In a full cascade failure on Express or Easy Auctions (the winning bidder and up to two subsequent bidders all default in sequence), all forfeited amounts are retained by the Platform; none is passed to the Market Maker. Full detail and worked examples appear in the Fee & Charges Schedule.

sections.title: 4. Withdrawing an Offer or Bid
sections.body:
4.1. Buy-Now: an offer may be withdrawn before the Market Maker accepts it, provided the Trader states a reason from the list provided in-app. No reason is required if the offer simply lapses unactioned after 3 days.

4.2. Easy and Express Auctions: once a bid is placed and the required EMD is pledged, it stands for the remainder of that Trading Session. There is no separate mid-auction bid withdrawal mechanism distinct from being outbid.

4.3. Tender Auction: withdrawal and its consequences are entirely as set by the Market Maker for that specific auction.

sections.title: 5. Listing & Trading Session Cancellation
sections.body:
5.1. A Market Maker may request a change to an approved Lot at any time; if an active Trading Session is attached, that session is cancelled and all active bids/deposits are refunded in full, with bidders notified. The Lot is then archived and a new version re-enters approval.

5.2. Once a Trading Session is live, it cannot be cancelled by the Market Maker directly (Express Auctions cannot be cancelled by the Market Maker at all). The TSX Master or Custodian may terminate any live session via an Emergency Stop, with a mandatory, logged reason, in which case all active bids/deposits are refunded in full.

sections.title: 6. Verified Lot Inspection Fee
sections.body: 6.1. The inspection fee for a Verified Lot is payable before inspection is scheduled.

sections.title: 7. How Refunds Are Paid
sections.body: 7.1. Refunds are paid to the account originally used to fund the deposit. A different payout account may only be used if it has been formally verified and any required cooling-off period has elapsed, per the Terms of Usage.

sections.title: 8. Contact
sections.body: Questions about a specific refund or forfeiture should be raised through our Dispute Resolution Process or directly with your TradeSphereX's support channel.

content.footer: See also our Fee & Charges Schedule and Terms of Usage.

content.title: Grievance Redressal Policy
content.meta: Adwiti Technocrats Pvt. Ltd · Effective Date: 15-September-2026 · Contact: Contact Us

sections.title: 1. Purpose & Scope
sections.body:
1.1. This Policy sets out how to raise a grievance about ADWITIX as a platform — distinct from a dispute about a specific Trading Session, which is handled under our separate Dispute Resolution Process.

1.2. A grievance may relate to matters such as: how your data has been handled, conduct by a TSX Master or platform staff, a concern about how a rule was applied to you, or dissatisfaction with the outcome of a prior support interaction.

sections.title: 2. Grievance Officer
sections.body: In accordance with the Information Technology Act 2000 and the rules made thereunder, the details of our Grievance Officer are available via our Contact Us page.

sections.title: 3. How to File a Grievance
sections.body:
3.1. A grievance may be submitted in writing, through the contact channel published on the Trust & Support section of the app, or directly to the Grievance Officer.

3.2. Please include: your registered mobile number, a description of the issue, and any relevant transaction or Lot reference.

sections.title: 4. Acknowledgement & Resolution Timelines
sections.body: 4.1. Grievances are acknowledged within 24 hours of receipt, and are resolved, or a substantive response provided, within 15 days.

sections.title: 5. Escalation Path
sections.body:
5.1. Most day-to-day concerns are resolved directly by your TradeSphereX's support team or TSX Master.

5.2. If unresolved, or if the concern relates to Custodian-level conduct, it is escalated to the Custodian.

5.3. If still unresolved, or if you are dissatisfied with the response, you may escalate directly to the Grievance Officer named in Section 2.

sections.title: 6. Your Right to External Recourse
sections.body: 6.1. Nothing in this Policy limits your right to approach a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, another applicable regulatory authority, or a court of competent jurisdiction, at any time.

content.title: Dispute Resolution Process
content.meta: A plain-language guide · Adwiti Technocrats Pvt. Ltd · Effective Date: 15-September-2026 · Contact: Contact Us

sections.title: 1. What This Covers
sections.body: This document explains, in plain language, how a disagreement about a specific Trading Session gets reviewed and resolved on ADWITIX. It applies to Buy-Now, Express, and Easy Auctions. Tender Auctions are excluded, since they run entirely on terms set directly by the Market Maker.

sections.title: 2. What Can Be Disputed
sections.body:
• Payment Dispute: one side says money was paid or received when the other side disagrees.
  • Condition/Delivery Dispute: the item received doesn't genuinely match what was described or shown.
  • Non-Lifting/Collection Dispute: a Trader won't collect an item, or a Market Maker is blocking collection.
  • Auction Rejection Dispute: a Market Maker rejected a winning result and you believe the reason given doesn't hold up.
  • Trader Non-Response Dispute: a Trader has gone silent on confirming or rating, holding up a Market Maker's settlement.

A sixth, internal process — Standing Review — looks at a Market Maker's overall pattern of conduct over time. This isn't something you file; it happens automatically based on accumulated history, and is explained in our governance documentation rather than here.

sections.title: 3. How to File
sections.body:
3.1. Open the transaction in question and select "Raise a Dispute." Choose the category that best matches your situation and provide a clear description.

3.2. Disputes must be filed within 7 days of the event that triggered them (for example, within 7 days of the expected delivery date, or of a rejected result).

sections.title: 4. Evidence
sections.body:
4.1. Once filed, both sides have a window to upload supporting evidence — photographs, messages, delivery records, payment proof, or anything else relevant.

4.2. A ruling is based only on the evidence submitted within this window, so it's worth submitting everything relevant promptly rather than waiting.

sections.title: 5. Who Decides
sections.body:
5.1. Most disputes are reviewed and ruled on by your TradeSphereX's own TSX Master, since they're closest to that TSX's transactions.

5.2. Disputes specifically about Trader non-response are reviewed directly by the Custodian.

5.3. Every ruling comes with a stated reason — you'll always know why a decision was made, not just what the decision was.

sections.title: 6. Timelines
sections.body: 6.1. We aim to resolve every dispute as quickly as the evidence allows, rather than holding it for a fixed period even once a decision is clear.

sections.title: 7. What Happens While a Dispute Is Open
sections.body: 7.1. A previously approved forfeiture or refund is not automatically paused just because a dispute has been filed against it — it proceeds on schedule. If the dispute is later decided in your favour, the outcome is corrected retroactively.

sections.title: 8. Appeal
sections.body:
8.1. If your dispute was decided by a TSX Master, you may appeal once, directly to the Custodian, whose decision is final.

8.2. Disputes decided directly by the Custodian are final and not open to further appeal within this process — though your right to seek external recourse (see our Grievance Redressal Policy) is unaffected.

sections.title: 9. Filing in Bad Faith
sections.body: 9.1. A pattern of repeated, unsubstantiated disputes is tracked and may itself lead to a consequence for the account filing them.

content.footer: See also our Grievance Redressal Policy and Star Ratings.

content.title: Terms of Use & Privacy Policy
content.meta: Adwiti Technocrats Pvt. Ltd · Effective Date: 15-September-2026 · Applies to every TradeSphereX operating on ADWITIX

sections.title: 1. Accounts & Roles
sections.body: You may hold multiple roles on ADWITIX — Trader, Market Maker, or both — under a single verified identity. Custodians are structurally barred from holding any participant role. A suspension or revoked compliance flag on your master KYC status cascades automatically to every role you hold.

sections.title: 2. Identity Verification (KYC)
sections.body: You must complete KYC before bidding or listing: document upload to an encrypted vault, Aadhaar tokenization, and PAN/GSTIN registry checks. Buyers are verified by the platform Custodian; Market Makers are verified by their TSX Master. Submitted KYC dossiers lock until a Verified or Suspended decision is issued.

sections.title: 3. Listings & Trading Sessions
sections.body: Every listing requires authentic, unedited media of the actual item — stock, catalogue, or generated imagery is never permitted absent an approved Tenant Media Waiver. Approved listings enter a limited post-approval edit window before parameters freeze for the live Trading Session.

sections.title: 4. Bidding, EMD & Settlement
sections.body: Bids constitute a binding commitment backed by an escrowed Earnest Money Deposit. Winning bidders and Market Makers must each submit a No Objection Certificate and a mandatory settlement rating before a deal is considered closed; unresponsive parties are subject to stall resolution and rating consequences.

sections.title: 5. Fees & Payment
sections.body: A Success Fee applies only on completed sales, on a declining schedule by final sale value, subject to a minimum of ₹500 + GST. Buyer-Pays is the default fee allocation; Seller-Pays is available on paid subscription tiers and, once selected for a Trading Session, is locked at bidding open.

sections.title: 6. Ratings, Standing & Rehabilitation
sections.body: Every account holds separate Trader and Market Maker star ratings, starting at 3★. A rating below 2★ triggers Crawl-Back — a temporary restriction to your tenant's Low value bracket. Persistently poor standing triggers Shadow Banning, a graduated reduction in platform-driven visibility rather than an outright block.

sections.title: 7. Disputes & Standing Review
sections.body: Disputes are filed against a specific transaction within a defined window, resolved with evidence from both sides and a stated rationale. Tenant Admin rulings may be appealed once, to the Custodian, whose decision is final. Market Makers are additionally subject to periodic Standing Review, opened annually or once complaints exceed a set threshold.

sections.title: 8. Payout Accounts
sections.body: Any change to your registered payout bank account requires OTP re-verification of the account holder and a mandatory 24-hour cooling-off period before the new account becomes active for settlements or refunds.

sections.title: 9. Data Handling & Privacy
sections.body: KYC documents are encrypted end-to-end; Aadhaar numbers are tokenized and never stored in plain text. Every material action is logged to a tamper-evident audit trail, retained for the statutory period applicable to your subscription tier. Consent is captured and logged individually at registration, KYC, and each EMD pledge.

content.desc: Every topic is explained twice — once for Traders, once for Market Makers — so you only read the half that applies to you.

items.q: How do I create an account?
items.buyer: Enter your mobile number and verify it with an OTP. Once verified, set a 4-digit mPIN — you'll use your number and mPIN to log in from then on.
items.seller: Same first step — every account starts as a Trader account. To list items, you then apply to a specific TradeSphereX and get approved by that TSX Master.

items.q: What documents do I need to verify my account?
items.buyer: Individuals: name, PAN, Aadhaar, date of birth, occupation. Businesses: company registration details (CIN, GST, PAN) and supporting documents. Verification is reviewed by a person, not an automated system.
items.seller: Same requirements as a Trader, since every Market Maker account is a Trader account first. Your TSX may also ask for category-specific documents.

items.q: How do I become a Market Maker?
items.buyer: Apply to sell through a specific TradeSphereX's storefront. Approval is scoped to that one TSX — approval on one doesn't carry over to another.
items.seller: You apply, the TSX Master reviews your request, and once approved you can start listing on that storefront. You can apply to multiple TSXs independently.

items.q: What is the EMD and why do I need one?
items.buyer: To bid or make an offer, you pledge 10% of the item's value upfront. It shows you're serious and stops people placing bids they never intend to honour.
items.seller: Market Makers only — Traders never pay a deposit to list or sell. This is what protects you from a winner walking away.

items.q: How do I add money to my account balance?
items.buyer: Transfer funds by bank transfer and upload the receipt. Once verified, the equivalent balance credits to your account for bidding anywhere on the platform.
items.seller: Not applicable — Market Makers don't need a balance to list items.

items.q: Do I get my deposit back if I don't win?
items.buyer: Yes. As soon as you're outbid or not selected, your deposit is released back to your balance immediately.
items.seller: Not applicable, since you never post a deposit.

items.q: Can my deposit be forfeited?
items.buyer: Yes — if you win and then fail to pay, your deposit is forfeited in full. This is treated seriously and affects your rating.
items.seller: If a Trader defaults after winning your Lot, their forfeited deposit generally passes to you as compensation, after the TSX's and platform's fee is taken out.

items.q: Do I pay extra if my payment method charges a fee?
items.buyer: Yes — a card processing charge is added on top of your deposit and shown clearly before you pay. Bank transfer or UPI usually carries little to no such charge.
items.seller: Not applicable to you, since you never pay a deposit.

items.q: What's the difference between Buy-Now, Express, Easy, and Tender?
items.buyer: Buy-Now: you offer and the Market Maker picks who to sell to. Express: fast, starts once 3 Traders join, closes within the hour. Easy: scheduled with a proper inspection window. Tender: fully private, invite-only, run directly by the Market Maker.
items.seller: Buy-Now lets you personally choose the best offer. Express gets you a fast sale once enough interest builds. Easy gives Traders time to inspect. Tender gives you complete control over participation.

items.q: Can I inspect an item before bidding?
items.buyer: Depends on the format. Easy Auctions give a proper inspection window (24 hours to 7 days). Express Auctions skip inspection — you bid on the listing photos and description alone.
items.seller: For Easy Auctions, you choose the inspection window (24 hours to 7 days). Express Auctions skip inspection entirely, in exchange for a much faster sale.

items.q: In Buy-Now, does the highest offer always win?
items.buyer: Not necessarily. The Market Maker can choose a lower offer from a Trader they trust more (based on your rating). If they do, they're required to record why.
items.seller: Yes — you're not locked into the highest number. You can factor in reliability. If you pick someone other than the top offer, you'll need to state a reason, kept on record.

items.q: If Express has no inspection, how do I know what I'm bidding on?
items.buyer: Every Express Lot includes a mandatory checklist the Market Maker fills out declaring known damage or missing parts. A false disclosure is treated as a genuine dispute.
items.seller: You're required to complete a defect-disclosure checklist before your Express Lot goes live. Answering it falsely can result in a dispute against you.

items.q: I won a Trading Session — what happens next?
items.buyer: If the final price is higher than your original deposit covered, you may need to top up first. Then you pay the Market Maker directly (offline) and arrange collection.
items.seller: Once a winner is confirmed, you deal with the Trader directly for payment and handover — the platform never holds the full sale amount, only the deposit.

items.q: What happens if the winning bidder doesn't pay?
items.buyer: If you win and don't pay within the required window, you forfeit your deposit and the win passes to the next-highest bidder.
items.seller: Non-paying winners are automatically replaced by the next-highest bidder. If every bidder fails to pay, the Trading Session is cancelled and you'll need to relist.

items.q: Can I lose my win to someone else?
items.buyer: No — once confirmed as winner and you pay on time, the sale is yours. You only lose a win by failing to pay in time.
items.seller: No — once a Trader completes payment on time, you can't reassign the sale.

items.q: How does the Star Rating system work?
items.buyer: You have your own Trader rating, separate from any Market Maker rating. Everyone starts at 3 stars. Paying promptly and completing deals cleanly raises it; defaulting or late payment lowers it.
items.seller: You have your own Market Maker rating, entirely separate from your Trader rating. Accurate listings and fast handovers raise it; mismatched descriptions or delays lower it.

items.q: Can my rating recover after a bad mark?
items.buyer: Yes. If your rating drops significantly, you enter Crawl-Back — temporarily limited to smaller-value purchases until a set number of clean transactions restores you.
items.seller: Yes, the same recovery path applies — a run of clean, accurate listings restores your standing over time.

items.q: What happens if my rating gets very low?
items.buyer: Very low-rated accounts are shown less (Shadow Banning) rather than blocked outright. You can still use the platform, just with less visibility.
items.seller: The same applies to your listings — a very low rating means your items stop being actively promoted, though still technically listed.

items.q: How do I actually pay or receive payment?
items.buyer: You pay the Market Maker directly — offline — for 100% of the sale value. The platform only ever holds your deposit.
items.seller: You're paid directly by the Trader, in full, outside the platform. Once received, you confirm it to move the deal toward closure.

items.q: What is an NOC and why do both sides need to file one?
items.buyer: You confirm receipt of goods, and the Market Maker confirms receipt of payment. A deal only closes once both confirm.
items.seller: You confirm receipt of payment, and the Trader confirms receipt of goods. Both are required before the deal closes and any remaining deposit is released.

items.q: What if the other party won't confirm?
items.buyer: If the Market Maker goes silent, you're sent a reminder, then a TSX Master steps in to review the facts and unstick the deal.
items.seller: The same reminder-then-admin-review process applies if a Trader goes silent on confirming or rating you.

items.q: Do I get an invoice for fees paid?
items.buyer: Yes — once a deal closes, an invoice covering the Success Fee (plus tax) is generated automatically.
items.seller: Yes — an invoice is generated for the TSX's commission share, accessible against the transaction record.

items.q: Why do I have to confirm something specific right before I pledge a deposit?
items.buyer: That acknowledgment spells out exactly what happens if you don't follow through on this specific bid — so you know the real consequence before committing.
items.seller: This doesn't apply to you directly since you never pledge a deposit — but the same idea protects you too.

items.q: What if the item doesn't match the listing?
items.buyer: For scheduled auctions, you're expected to inspect beforehand, so ordinary condition complaints after winning aren't valid. Genuine fraud or material misrepresentation can still be disputed.
items.seller: Traders waive routine condition complaints once they've had an inspection opportunity — but genuine misrepresentation can still be disputed, so accurate listings matter.

items.q: How do I file a dispute?
items.buyer: Raise it against the specific Trading Session, choose the fitting category, and submit evidence within the filing window.
items.seller: Same process — file against the transaction, select a category, submit evidence. Both sides get an equal window to respond.

items.q: Who decides the outcome of a dispute?
items.buyer: Most disputes are reviewed by the TSX Master; disputes about Trader conduct go to Custodian-level review. Every decision comes with a stated reason and one appeal.
items.seller: Same structure applies — disputes about your conduct are typically reviewed by the TSX Master, with a documented reason and one appeal right.

items.q: Can items be grouped and browsed together?
items.buyer: Yes — Lots sharing a common origin are tagged and shown together on one screen, even though each is still its own independent sale.
items.seller: You can tag multiple related Lots as a group so Traders see them together, while each still sells completely independently.

items.q: What are the photo and video requirements for a Lot?
items.buyer: Every Lot needs real photos of the actual item — never stock images. Photos and video are automatically optimised for fast loading.
items.seller: You need at least 5 real photos (up to 50), with one as the main photo. Video is optional, up to 2 minutes, compressed automatically after upload.

items.q: Does the Market Maker have to arrange shipping?
items.buyer: No — shipping is always optional. You can always self-collect at no extra cost.
items.seller: You can offer shipping if you want, but it's never required — Traders can always self-collect instead.

items.q: Is there a limit on how much a bid can jump?
items.buyer: Yes — no bid can be more than 150% of the current highest bid, catching typing mistakes before they cause real problems.
items.seller: The same limit protects your Trading Session from being disrupted by an obviously mistaken or malicious bid.

items.q: How does the platform stop last-second sniping?
items.buyer: A bid landing in the final 10 minutes extends the Trading Session by 2 more minutes, giving everyone a fair chance to respond.
items.seller: The same rule protects your sale from closing on an artificially timed last-second bid.

items.q: How does the platform prevent fake or misleading photos?
items.buyer: Photos are captured through the app itself at the moment of listing, with location and time data attached — not uploaded from an old gallery.
items.seller: This in-app capture requirement protects you too — clear evidence the photos are genuinely of your item.

content.desc: Plain-language definitions for every ADWITIX-specific term you'll come across as a Trader or Market Maker.

terms.def: What happens when a winning Trader doesn't pay: the win passes to the next-highest Trader at their own price, within their own time window. This can happen up to three times before a Trading Session is cancelled outright.
A safety limit stopping any single bid from jumping more than 150% above the current price — catches typing mistakes and blocks deliberate price manipulation.
A sale format where Traders make offers and the Market Maker personally chooses who to sell to, considering price and the Trader's rating — not necessarily the highest offer.
Short for Category-Location-Value — the set of preferences that personalises which Lots and alerts you see.

A Lot where the Market Maker has taken their own photos, by any method. Real, unedited photos of the actual item are required — stock or generated images are never allowed. Contrast with Verified Lot.
A recovery path for a Trader whose rating has dropped significantly — temporarily limited to smaller purchases until a set number of clean transactions restores their standing.
The formal process for resolving a disagreement about a specific Trading Session — filed by a Trader or Market Maker, reviewed with evidence from both sides, and decided with a stated reason.
A rule that extends a Trading Session by a short period whenever a bid lands in the closing minutes, so a last-second bid can't unfairly end it before others can respond.

A scheduled auction with a real inspection window (set by the Market Maker, 24 hours to 7 days) before bidding opens. The Market Maker can choose whether results close instantly or need their approval.
The refundable deposit — 10% of the item's value — a Trader must pledge before placing a bid or offer. Returned automatically unless they win and then fail to pay.
The price a Market Maker states as their target/asking figure in a Buy-Now Lot. Traders may offer above or below it — it's a reference point, not a hard limit.
The fastest sale format — no inspection window at all. The Trading Session only starts once exactly 3 Traders have pledged a deposit, then runs for about an hour.

The loss of a Trader's deposit after winning a Trading Session and then failing to complete payment. In most cases the money goes to the Market Maker as compensation; in a full cascading default, it doesn't.
The process for raising a broader concern about the platform itself — separate from a dispute about one specific Trading Session.
Shorthand for the highest, second-highest, and third-highest bidder in a Trading Session at the moment it closes. If H1 defaults, the win passes to H2, then H3.
Know Your Customer — the identity verification every user completes before transacting, using documents like PAN and Aadhaar (individuals) or company registration details (businesses).
The real-time scrolling feed showing your account balance, the status of your active bids, and new Lots matching your interests.
The platform's internal representation of deposited funds — always equal in value to what you deposited (1:1), held as a distinct amount tied to each specific bid, not one shared spendable balance.
A digital confirmation both sides must submit before a deal is considered closed — the Market Maker confirms they were paid, the Trader confirms they received the goods.
A processing fee some payment methods (like cards) carry, added on top of your deposit so the full deposit amount still reaches escrow untouched.
Multiple Lots that share a common origin (e.g., items from the same site) shown together on one screen for convenience — while each one remains a fully separate, independent sale.
The confidential floor price a Market Maker sets for an Easy or Express Auction. The item won't sell for less than this, and it's what a Trader's deposit is calculated against.
The platform's top-level administrator, who oversees the whole system but never personally trades, lists, or has any visibility into a live Trading Session while it's happening.
Your reputation score specifically as a Market Maker — separate from your Trader rating, even if you do both.
The final stage of a completed sale: the Trader pays the Market Maker directly, both confirm their side (NOC), both rate each other, and any remaining deposit is refunded.
A gradual reduction in visibility (fewer alerts, less promotion) for an account with a persistently poor rating — not a full block, just reduced platform support.
A periodic, big-picture check on a Market Maker's overall conduct — triggered either once a year, or sooner if enough complaints build up.
Your reputation score, starting at 3 out of 5, that rises with clean, on-time transactions and falls with defaults or disputes. Traders and Market Makers each have their own, separate score.
An individual storefront operating on ADWITIX under its own branding — could be a bank, an institution, or the platform's own general marketplace.
The person a TradeSphereX has authorised to approve Lots, set local terms, and manage Market Makers on that specific storefront.
A fully private, invite-only sale format where the Market Maker personally controls who can participate and on what terms — available only through the platform's own operated shop.
A Lot where ADWITIX's own inspection team has visited the item and taken the photos themselves. Contrast with Certified by Seller.

content.desc: A practical guide for Traders and Market Makers. Everything here reflects ADWITIX's actual rules — when in doubt, the safer choice is almost always the one on the left.

rows.do: Register with your own genuine mobile number and complete KYC honestly and fully.
rows.dont: Create multiple accounts, or register using someone else's details.

rows.do: Keep your 4-digit mPIN private, and treat it like a banking PIN.
rows.dont: Share your mPIN or OTP with anyone — not even someone claiming to be ADWITIX support.

rows.do: Apply to a specific TradeSphereX if you want to sell, and wait for approval.
rows.dont: Assume selling approval on one TSX lets you sell on another.

rows.do: Read the terms shown before you accept them, especially around a specific bid or deposit.
rows.dont: Click through consent screens without reading — they describe real, binding commitments.

rows.do: Only bid or offer on items you genuinely intend to buy if you win.
rows.dont: Bid casually or "just to see" — every bid pledges real money and carries real consequences.

rows.do: Check your available balance before bidding, so you're not caught short on a required top-up.
rows.dont: Assume you can back out painlessly after winning — a default forfeits your deposit.

rows.do: Read the specific forfeiture terms shown before you pledge a deposit.
rows.dont: Ignore the acknowledgment shown before each pledge — it states exactly what you're agreeing to for that bid.

rows.do: Use bank transfer or UPI where possible for depositing funds.
rows.dont: Rely on a card payment if a bank-transfer option is available and convenient.

rows.do: Inspect the item during the window provided, for formats that offer one (Easy Auctions, Buy-Now).
rows.dont: Expect an inspection window on Express Auctions — that format is sight-unseen by design.

rows.do: Review a Market Maker's rating and listing details carefully before committing.
rows.dont: Assume the highest bid always wins in Buy-Now — the Market Maker can choose based on reliability, not just price.

rows.do: Raise a genuine concern about fraud or major misrepresentation promptly.
rows.dont: Dispute an item's general condition after winning if you had a fair chance to inspect it first.

rows.do: Complete payment within the required window if you win.
rows.dont: Delay payment or go silent after winning — non-payment forfeits your deposit and damages your rating.

rows.do: Upload real, current photographs of the actual item, taken through the app.
rows.dont: Use stock photos, old images, or photos of a different (even similar) item.

rows.do: Describe the item's condition accurately, including known flaws.
rows.dont: Overstate condition or omit known defects — this can trigger a dispute and a rating penalty, even sight-unseen on Express.

rows.do: Set your Reserve Value at a realistic, defensible level.
rows.dont: Set an unrealistically low Reserve Value hoping to profit from bidder defaults — full-cascade failures pay Market Makers nothing.

rows.do: Respond promptly to Trader questions and to your TSX's review process.
rows.dont: Ignore listing rejection feedback — check the stated reason and correct it before resubmitting.

rows.do: Pay/collect the full sale amount directly and promptly once a deal is won.
rows.dont: Try to negotiate a different amount or route the payment outside what was agreed on the listing.

rows.do: Confirm receipt (goods or funds) as soon as it genuinely happens.
rows.dont: Delay confirming receipt — this holds up the other party's refund and can trigger an admin review of you.

rows.do: Rate the other party honestly and promptly once the deal is done.
rows.dont: Skip or ignore the rating step — both sides rating each other is required to close the deal.

rows.do: Build your rating through consistent, honest, on-time transactions.
rows.dont: Expect a single good transaction to erase a pattern of poor ones.

rows.do: Take a rating drop seriously and use the Crawl-Back path available to you.
rows.dont: Assume a low rating is permanent — a defined run of clean transactions restores standing over time.

rows.do: Remember your Trader★ and Market Maker★ are separate — build both deliberately if you do both.
rows.dont: Assume being a great Market Maker automatically makes you look trustworthy as a Trader, or vice versa.

rows.do: File a dispute promptly, within the stated window, with real supporting evidence.
rows.dont: Wait past the filing window and then expect a dispute to still be accepted.

rows.do: Choose the dispute category that genuinely matches your situation.
rows.dont: File repeated, weak, or baseless disputes — this pattern is tracked and can itself count against you.

rows.do: Accept a ruling's stated reasoning, or use the appeal path if you genuinely disagree.
rows.dont: Assume every ruling can be appealed indefinitely — most rulings allow exactly one appeal.

rows.do: Verify your identity again if asked, especially before a payout bank change.
rows.dont: Be surprised by a short waiting period after changing your payout account — it's a fraud-prevention step.

rows.do: Report any suspicious account activity immediately.
rows.dont: Reuse your ADWITIX mPIN as a password anywhere else.

rows.do: Expect a payment-method charge to be shown clearly before you pay, if one applies.
rows.dont: Assume every payment method costs the same — bank transfer/UPI is usually cheaper and faster.

rows.do: Agree on collection or shipping terms clearly before the deal proceeds.
rows.dont: Assume shipping is included by default — self-collection is the baseline unless otherwise agreed.

rows.do: Keep records (photos, messages, receipts) of the handover.
rows.dont: Rely on memory alone if a dispute becomes possible — evidence submitted within the window is what a ruling is based on.

content.desc: A plain explanation of how your money, your data, and your Trading Sessions are protected on ADWITIX — and how we hold ourselves accountable.

pillars.title: Your Money Is Never Pooled
pillars.intro: Every deposit you pledge is held separately, tied to the specific bid it secures — never mixed into one shared pot with other Traders' money.
points: Each deposit is a distinct, ring-fenced holding, released or forfeited only based on that specific Trading Session's outcome.
Your deposit is refunded automatically as soon as it's no longer needed — outbid, not selected, or deal closed — with no fixed delay.
No interest is ever taken from money held on your behalf.
Deposits are held through a licensed, RBI-regulated payment partner, not an unlicensed wallet.

pillars.title: Your Data Is Protected
pillars.intro: Sensitive information is encrypted, minimised, and shared only with whoever genuinely needs it, only when they need it.
points: Aadhaar and other sensitive ID data are stored in masked, tokenised form — never in plain text.
Banking details are encrypted and used solely to process refunds and settlements.
Your identity stays hidden from a counterparty until a real commitment is made on both sides — not shared upfront.
We never sell your data to anyone, for any reason.

pillars.title: What You See Is Real
pillars.intro: Lots are built from genuine, verifiable evidence — not stock photos or recycled images.
points: Every photo is captured through the app itself, at the moment of listing — not uploaded from an old gallery.
Location and timestamp data is captured automatically alongside each photo, making it far harder to pass off a fake or unrelated image.
Stock photography and placeholder images are never allowed on a Lot.
Even on Express Auctions, Market Makers must disclose any known defects upfront — not just what the photos happen to show.

pillars.title: A Level Playing Field
pillars.intro: The bidding process is designed so no one — including us — gets an unfair edge.
points: During a live Trading Session, nobody can see who else is bidding — not other Traders, not the Market Maker.
Even our Custodian has zero visibility into a Trading Session while it's actually happening — access opens only after it closes, same as everyone else.
No single bid can jump more than 150% above the current price, catching costly typos and blocking deliberate price manipulation.
Bidding activity is continuously monitored for patterns that suggest manipulation or bad-faith behaviour.

pillars.title: Every Action Is Accountable
pillars.intro: Decisions that affect you always come with a stated reason and a permanent record — never a silent, unexplained outcome.
points: Every rejection, forfeiture, and dispute ruling is logged with the specific reason behind it.
Records in our system can't be secretly altered — not by outside parties, and not by our own staff.
Before you pledge a deposit, you're shown a clear, specific summary of what you're agreeing to for that exact bid.
A rating can only drop significantly after a human review — never an automatic, unchecked penalty — and you always have the right to appeal.

pillars.title: Independently Checked
pillars.intro: We don't just tell you the platform is secure — it's regularly verified by people outside our own team.
points: The platform undergoes independent security audits by outside specialists, not just our own developers.
Our servers' clocks are continuously synced and monitored, so Trading Session timing can't be secretly manipulated.
Unusual money-movement patterns are actively monitored to guard against misuse of the platform.
Our payment infrastructure runs through a licensed, RBI-authorised partner, not an in-house or unregulated system.
